The **Pro Kabaddi League**, abbreviated as **PKL**, is an Indian men's [kabaddi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabaddi "Kabaddi") league.[[1]](#cite_note-1) It premiered in 2014 and airs on [Star Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Sports_(Indian_TV_network) "Star Sports (Indian TV network)").[[2]](#cite_note-2) It is the most popular kabaddi league in the world and the second most watched sports league in [India](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/India "India") after the [cricket](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Cricket "Cricket") league [Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League").[[3]](#cite_note-3)

Since its inception there have been eight different champions. [Patna Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patna_Pirates "Patna Pirates") have won the league three consecutive times. [Jaipur Pink Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur_Pink_Panthers "Jaipur Pink Panthers") and [Dabang Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dabang_Delhi_K.C. "Dabang Delhi K.C.") have won twice each, while [U Mumba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U_Mumba "U Mumba"), [Bengaluru Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengaluru_Bulls "Bengaluru Bulls"), [Bengal Warriorz](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Warriorz "Bengal Warriorz"), [Puneri Paltan](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Puneri_Paltan "Puneri Paltan") and [Haryana Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haryana_Steelers "Haryana Steelers") have one title each. Dabang Delhi are the current champions after winning their second title in the [2025 edition](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2025_Pro_Kabaddi_League "2025 Pro Kabaddi League").

The league's inception was influenced by the popularity of the kabaddi tournament at the [2006 Asian Games](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2006_Asian_Games "2006 Asian Games"). The Pro Kabaddi League uses a franchise-based model and its first season was held in 2014 with eight teams each of which has paid fees of up to US$250,000 (₹20,00,000) to join.[[4]](#cite_note-bbc-kabaddiipl-4)[[5]](#cite_note-5)

There were doubts over whether the Pro Kabaddi League would be successful, noting that many leagues were attempting to emulate the IPL's business model and success and that, unlike cricket, there were relatively fewer well-known players in Kabaddi. However, it was also noted that kabaddi was widely played in grassroots community settings, and could thus attract a wide variety of rural and metropolitan viewers for advertisers to target if the league gained significant attraction.[[4]](#cite_note-bbc-kabaddiipl-4)

The inaugural season was seen by 43.5 [crores](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Crore "Crore") (435 million) viewers, second to the [2014 Indian Premier League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Indian_Premier_League "2014 Indian Premier League")'s 55.2 crores (552 million), while the first season final between [Jaipur Pink Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur_Pink_Panthers "Jaipur Pink Panthers") and [U-Mumba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U_Mumba "U Mumba") was watched by 8.64 crores (86.4 million).[[6]](#cite_note-thehindu-pklratings-6)[[7]](#cite_note-guardian-kabaddiwc-7) [Star Sports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Star_Sports_(Indian_TV_network) "Star Sports (Indian TV network)"), the Pro Kabaddi League's broadcaster,[[8]](#cite_note-indiatimes1-8) subsequently announced in 2015 that it would acquire a 74% stake in the league's parent company Mashal Sports.[[9]](#cite_note-9)

For the [2017](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Pro_Kabaddi_League_season "2017 Pro Kabaddi League season") and [2018–19](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2018–19_Pro_Kabaddi_League_season "2018–19 Pro Kabaddi League season") season, the Pro Kabaddi League added four new teams, and changed its format to split the teams into two divisions known as "zones".[[10]](#cite_note-10) Soon the league returned to its regular double round-robin format from the [2019](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Pro_Kabaddi_League_season "2019 Pro Kabaddi League season") season.

The league won the Best Sports League at the [Confederation of Indian Industry](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Confederation_of_Indian_Industry "Confederation of Indian Industry") Sports Business Awards in 2024 at [New Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/New_Delhi "New Delhi").[[11]](#cite_note-11)

## Format

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Pro_Kabaddi_League&action=edit&section=2 "Edit section: Format")]

The Pro Kabaddi League follows a round-robin format, where each team plays against 6 teams twice and 6 teams once during the league phase.

At the end of the league phase, the top 4 teams qualify for the playoffs, while the teams ranking from position 5 to 8 qualify for the play-ins. The playoffs and play-ins consist of eliminators and finals where teams compete to reach the ultimate final match. The team that wins the final is crowned the champion of the Pro Kabaddi League.

The league has various individual awards like the Most Valuable Player aka MVP, Best Raider, and Best Defender, among others, to recognize outstanding performances of players during the season.

### Season 1 (2014)

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Pro_Kabaddi_League&action=edit&section=4 "Edit section: Season 1 (2014)")]

Main article: [2014 Pro Kabaddi League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2014_Pro_Kabaddi_League "2014 Pro Kabaddi League")

The first signing and auction of players for the 8 teams were held on 20 May 2014[[8]](#cite_note-indiatimes1-8) in [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"). India's national kabaddi captain [Rakesh Kumar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Rakesh_Kumar_(kabaddi) "Rakesh Kumar (kabaddi)") was the priciest among the players bought for ₹12.80 lakh by the [Patna Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patna_Pirates "Patna Pirates").[[12]](#cite_note-thehindu-12) Sports Authority of India's [Deepak Niwas Hooda](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Deepak_Niwas_Hooda "Deepak Niwas Hooda") was bought by the Telugu Titans franchise for ₹12.60 lakh.[[12]](#cite_note-thehindu-12) Tae Deok Eom was the highest paid overseas player bought for ₹7 lakh by the Patna franchise.[[12]](#cite_note-thehindu-12)

The duration of the season was from 26 July 2014 to 31 August 2014. There were double round-robin matches along with two semifinals, third place and final games. 56 games were to be played in the first round and 4 in the playoff stage, making a total of 60 games. 8 teams took part in the first edition. The first game was played on 26 July between [U Mumba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U_Mumba "U Mumba") and [Jaipur Pink Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur_Pink_Panthers "Jaipur Pink Panthers") and the final was played on 31 August at [Mumbai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mumbai "Mumbai"). [Jaipur Pink Panthers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jaipur_Pink_Panthers "Jaipur Pink Panthers") beat [U Mumba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U_Mumba "U Mumba") by 35–24 to win the inaugural Pro Kabaddi League.

### Season 2 (2015)

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Pro_Kabaddi_League&action=edit&section=5 "Edit section: Season 2 (2015)")]

Main article: [2015 Pro Kabaddi League](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2015_Pro_Kabaddi_League "2015 Pro Kabaddi League")

Star Sports Pro Kabaddi season 2 was from 18 July 2015 to 23 August 2015. There were 60 matches played with two semifinals, a third-place play-off and a final. ### Season 5 (2017)

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Pro_Kabaddi_League&action=edit&section=8 "Edit section: Season 5 (2017)")]

Main article: [2017 Pro Kabaddi League season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2017_Pro_Kabaddi_League_season "2017 Pro Kabaddi League season")

The 2017 season was the fifth edition of the Pro Kabaddi League, and it featured 12 teams, including new teams from [Uttar Pradesh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Uttar_Pradesh "Uttar Pradesh"), [Haryana](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haryana "Haryana"), [Tamil Nadu](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Nadu "Tamil Nadu"), and [Gujarat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat "Gujarat"). The team from Haryana is known as [Haryana Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haryana_Steelers "Haryana Steelers") owned by JSW Sports.[[15]](#cite_note-15) [Sachin Tendulkar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sachin_Tendulkar "Sachin Tendulkar") co-owns the Tamil Nadu team named [Tamil Thalaivas](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tamil_Thalaivas "Tamil Thalaivas").[[16]](#cite_note-16) The Uttar Pradesh team is named as [UP Yoddha](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/UP_Yoddha "UP Yoddha") owned by GMR group and the Gujarat team is named as [Gujarat Fortune Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Giants_(kabaddi) "Gujarat Giants (kabaddi)") owned by [Gautam Adani](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gautam_Adani "Gautam Adani").

Auctions for the new season were held in May, before which the existing teams were allowed to retain one player each. The auction saw over 400 players go under the hammer and ₹46.99 crores spent by the 12 teams.[[17]](#cite_note-17)

The Pro Kabaddi League season 5 started on 28 July 2017.

The most expensive pick of the auction was raider [Nitin Tomar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Nitin_Tomar "Nitin Tomar"), who was bought by the Uttar Pradesh team for a sum of ₹93 lakh. Following in second place was Rohit Kumar after the [Bengaluru Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengaluru_Bulls "Bengaluru Bulls") picked him for an ₹81 lakhs price. The most expensive foreign player was South Korea's [Lee Jang-kun](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lee_Jang-kun "Lee Jang-kun") after he was retained by the [Bengal Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Warriors "Bengal Warriors") for ₹80.3 lakhs.

The new season was slated to be the biggest league tournament of its kind in the history of Indian sports in terms of geographical coverage and duration. It featured 138 matches spread across a time period of 13 weeks across 11 states.

A children's Kabaddi tournament, known as [KBD Juniors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KBD_Juniors "KBD Juniors"), was also organised between schools of the cities in which the matches were held.

[Patna Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patna_Pirates "Patna Pirates") beat [Gujarat Fortune Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Giants_(kabaddi) "Gujarat Giants (kabaddi)") by 55–38 in the final with the Man of the Tournament [Pardeep Narwal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pardeep_Narwal "Pardeep Narwal") stealing the show with 19 raid points against the Fortune Giants defence for the first time in the tournament.

The award ceremony of the finale was hosted by Pooja Bhamrah. Pardeep Narwal was adjudged the man of the finale.

The 2018 season is the sixth edition of the Pro Kabaddi League, and it features 12 teams. Auctions for the new season were held in which [Haryana Steelers](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Haryana_Steelers "Haryana Steelers") paid ₹1.51 crores for Monu Goyat[[18]](#cite_note-18) who became the highest paid player in the history of Pro Kabaddi league.

The most expensive foreign player this season is [Fazel Atrachali](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Fazel_Atrachali "Fazel Atrachali")[[19]](#cite_note-19) from [Iran](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Iran "Iran"). He was bought by [U Mumba](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/U_Mumba "U Mumba") for ₹1 crore.

Zone B toppers, [Bengaluru Bulls](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengaluru_Bulls "Bengaluru Bulls") beat the Zone A toppers, [Gujarat Fortune Giants](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Gujarat_Giants_(kabaddi) "Gujarat Giants (kabaddi)") by 38–33 in the final with the Man of the Tournament Pawan Kumar Sehrawat stealing the show with a record 22 raid points against the young Fortune Giants defence. For a consecutive second time, Gujarat Fortune Giants have lost in the finals. The coach of Bengaluru Bulls, Randhir Singh was happy as his team finally won the tournament after underwhelming finishes in the previous couple of seasons. ### Season 7 (2019)

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Pro_Kabaddi_League&action=edit&section=10 "Edit section: Season 7 (2019)")]

Main article: [2019 Pro Kabaddi League season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2019_Pro_Kabaddi_League_season "2019 Pro Kabaddi League season")

The 2019 season is the seventh edition of the Pro Kabaddi League, and it features 12 teams. Auctions for the new season were held in Mumbai on 8 and 9 April. The franchises splashed out over 50 crores to acquire 200 players. [Siddharth Sirish Desai](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Siddharth_Sirish_Desai "Siddharth Sirish Desai") became the most expensive buy of the season after [Telugu Titans](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telugu_Titans "Telugu Titans") got the winning bid of him at ₹1.45 crore.[[20]](#cite_note-20) The most expensive foreign player of this season was Iranian [Mohammad Esmaeil Nabibakhsh](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohammad_Esmaeil_Nabibakhsh "Mohammad Esmaeil Nabibakhsh") who was bought by [Bengal Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Warriors "Bengal Warriors") for ₹77.75 lakh.[[21]](#cite_note-21) As termed by the organisers 'Most Toughest Season', the zonal system present in the previous season is removed, and each team will play against all the other teams twice. Top 6 teams will qualify for the playoffs. The top two teams will automatically make the semi-finals while the remaining four will battle it out in eliminators.[[22]](#cite_note-22) [Dabang Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dabang_Delhi "Dabang Delhi") and [Bengal Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Warriors "Bengal Warriors") emerged as the winners in the semi-finals and qualified to the final for the first time.[[23]](#cite_note-23)[[24]](#cite_note-24) In the final, [Bengal Warriors](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bengal_Warriors "Bengal Warriors") outplayed [Dabang Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dabang_Delhi "Dabang Delhi") by a margin of 39–34 and clinched their maiden Pro Kabaddi League title.[[25]](#cite_note-25)[[26]](#cite_note-26) The season witnessed several records. [Pardeep Narwal](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pardeep_Narwal "Pardeep Narwal") became the first ever player to reach 1000 points in the Pro Kabaddi League.[[27]](#cite_note-27) Naveen Kumar scored 21 consecutive Super 10s and overall 22.[[28]](#cite_note-28) While [Pawan Sehrawat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pawan_Sehrawat "Pawan Sehrawat") registered most individual points in a match (39) against Haryana Steelers.[[29]](#cite_note-29) In this season, for the first time three raiders crossed the 300-raid points mark.[[30]](#cite_note-30) Among the defenders, Neeraj Kumar of [Patna Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patna_Pirates "Patna Pirates") scored most tackle points (11) in a match and equalled the record of [Mohit Chillar](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mohit_Chillar "Mohit Chillar") (11).[[31]](#cite_note-31)

### Season 8 (2021)

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Pro_Kabaddi_League&action=edit&section=11 "Edit section: Season 8 (2021)")]

Main article: [2021-22 Pro Kabaddi League season](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2021-22_Pro_Kabaddi_League_season "2021-22 Pro Kabaddi League season")

The 2021–22 season is the eighth edition of Pro Kabaddi League. The season began on 22 December 2021. The usual travelling caravan format was changed to a single venue hosting all the matches of the season. Kanteerava Indoor Stadium, Bangalore was initially announced as the venue, but was later changed to the Sheraton Grand Hotel and Convention Center located in [Whitefield, Bangalore](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Whitefield,_Bangalore "Whitefield, Bangalore").[[32]](#cite_note-32) [Dabang Delhi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dabang_Delhi "Dabang Delhi") beat [Patna Pirates](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Patna_Pirates "Patna Pirates") in final to win their maiden PKL title. Naveen Kumar from Delhi created history by winning 2 back to back MVP awards. Bengaluru skipper [Pawan Sehrawat](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pawan_Sehrawat "Pawan Sehrawat") successfully defended his best raider crown and won the award for second season in a row. Sehrawat finished the campaign with 18 super raids and 304 raid points to his name. Iranian left corner, Mohammadreza chiyaneh from team Patna Pirates took the best defender award home for second season in a row. The rookie set a new PKL record with 10 High 5's and 89 tackle points. Mohit Goyat from pune was named the best new young player.

## Viewership

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Pro_Kabaddi_League&action=edit&section=16 "Edit section: Viewership")]

As per the available data of the opening two weeks, Star Sports Pro Kabaddi viewership on TV increased by nearly 56% from the 2014 year's viewership. During the inaugural season, viewership was 43.5 crore (435 million) viewers, which was the second in India after the 56 crore (560 million) of [IPL](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Indian_Premier_League "Indian Premier League") viewership. The online viewership also increased 1.3 crore unique visitors, which is 18.5 times than of last year's 7 lakh unique visitors. The third season which was flagged off on 30 January, recorded a surge in viewership with the opening week ratings 36 per cent higher than the week one viewership for its last season.[[42]](#cite_note-42)

In 10th season of PKL, the viewership registered 17% growth over the 9th season. It recorded 38 billion minutes of watch time (15% over 9th season).[[43]](#cite_note-43)

## Prize money

[[edit](/w/index.php?title=Pro_Kabaddi_League&action=edit&section=55 "Edit section: Prize money")]

Prize money for the winner of season 6 was ₹3 crore. The first and second runners-up were awarded ₹1.80 crore and ₹1.20 crore respectively.[[76]](#cite_note-76) The consolidated prize money for season 7 was ₹8 crore. The champions of season 7 bagged ₹3 crore while the runners-up received ₹1.8 crore. The losing semifinalists received ₹90 lakh each and, the fifth and the sixth-placed teams earned ₹45 lakh.[[77]](#cite_note-77)
